sets.title: Authorization decision: rule re-expression in compound predicates
sets.description: The same resource-authorization decision in three semantically equivalent forms: carrier A uses the pristine guard-clause form, carrier B re-expresses the same logic as compound rule predicates with combined condition grouping (sem_rule variant), and carrier C uses a different normalization order for grant checks (sem_normalization_order variant). All three compute behaviorally identical results. No two carriers share a token run long enough for token/line tools to pair them, so only semantic detection is expected to recover the cluster.
sets.notes: Set 001 of 5. SEM-01 variant (sem_rule) combines separate checks into compound predicates. SEM-11 variant (sem_normalization_order) reorders grant checks. Behavioral equivalence enforced by gen/seeds/access_guard/equivalence_test.php.

sets.title: Authorization decision: minimal two-idiom age check
sets.description: G-5 gap-fill: Minimal two-idiom age check before the full five-idiom spread. The same age-verification decision expressed as '$age >= 18' (carrier A, pristine) vs '!($age < 18)' (carrier B, De Morgan transformation). This is the simplest possible semantic rule variation — a single boolean logic transformation — before tackling the full multi-idiom complex predicates in rungs 1-5.
sets.notes: G-5 gap-fill: rung-1 minimal = the two-idiom age check ($age >= 18 vs !($age < 18)) before the full five-idiom spread. This demonstrates the simplest semantic equivalence pair — a single boolean law transformation.
